subject: Inquiry: PHI proxying via Redwood hosted vs dedicated — evidence & DPA
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurelia.health>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@aurelia.health, legal@aurelia.health
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: PHI proxying via Redwood hosted vs dedicated — evidence & DPA

Hi Priya,

Quick intro — I run platform at Aurelia Health. We're evaluating Redwood for a demo NLP pipeline that would extract structured problem lists from clinician notes. Our current flow is: partner webhooks -> our proxy service -> Redwood inference (POST payloads). A few security/compliance clarifications before we proceed: 

- If we forward patient identifiers and clinical notes to the hosted Redwood API, do you consider that PHI processing and require a BAA?
- What logging/retention behavior occurs by default for hosted customers? Are request/response full-text logs persisted, and can we opt-out or redact before storage?
- Are there managed DLP/tokenization features (prefix stripping, PII filters) or do you recommend client-side pseudonymization?
- For our legal team: can you provide SOC 2 Type II evidence, CAIQ/SIG exports, and a draft DPA/BAA? We also want an architecture stub that shows typical controls for a hosted vs Dedicated deployment.

Timing: we need evidence for an internal security review next week. Is a 48-hour turnaround realistic?

Thanks — happy to share more details or jump on a short call.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, Aurelia Health
samira.khan@aurelia.health
+1 (415) 555-0146

Subject: Re: Inquiry: PHI proxying via Redwood hosted vs dedicated — evidence & DPA

Hi Samira — thanks for the detailed note and the context, this is exactly the kind of information we need. High level answers up front, details and attachments to follow from our compliance team: 

- Yes — forwarding patient identifiers + notes to Redwood is treated as PHI processing and we require an executed BAA for any customer-side PHI workflows on hosted.
- Hosted customers can process PHI, but there are onboarding controls we require (DPA/BAA signature, PHI-mode configuration, retention settings). Dedicated or Private deployments provide stronger isolation (tenant-level log partitioning, dedicated GPU pools) and are commonly recommended for regulated workloads.
- We offer a combination of server-side redaction toggles and recommended client-side pseudonymization SDKs. By default hosted requests are logged in encrypted telemetry; you can enable a "do not persist" mode for request payloads at onboarding.

Kimberly and Dev — can you attach SOC2/CAIQ/SIG exports, the current DPA draft, a short architecture stub (ingest -> proxy recommendations), and a sample set of redaction rules? Samira — if you can confirm whether your proxy currently strips identifiers from URL paths and whether you POST JSON bodies (not GETs), we'll tailor the guidance.

I can coordinate and get a packet to you within 48 hours; for anything that needs legal review (DPA tweaks/BAA signature), we'll route that via our legal ops and usually have a turnaround of ~3 business days depending on redlines.

Would you be available for a 30-minute technical sync Thursday morning (May 27) PT?

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
SVP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Answering Aurelia PHI questions + attachments

Priya / team — attaching the packet for Samira. See short answers below we should use in our reply (and attach files listed):

Attachments included: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, redwood_caiq_export.zip, redwood_dpa_draft_2027-05-22.docx, ingest-architecture.png, sample-redaction-rules.txt

Short Q&A draft (use in outward message):
- BAA eligibility: Redwood will sign a BAA for customers who enable PHI workflows. For hosted customers we require the DPA + explicit PHI onboarding (a toggle in the Console). Once enabled, request payload persistence is disabled by default for the "PHI mode" unless the customer opts into retention for debugging; retention windows are configurable (30/90/180 days) and stored encrypted with customer-managed KMS available on Dedicated/Private tiers.

- Logging & retention: by default hosted request metadata (non-text tokens) is retained for observability; full-text request/response logs are encrypted and can be set to "do not persist". Access to logs is gated by RBAC and requires justification for production incidents. Dedicated provides tenant-level log partitioning and stronger separation; Private ensures data stays in customer VPC or on-prem.

- DLP/tokenization: we provide server-side redaction toggles (prefix stripping, remove SSNs, email normalization) and publish recommended client-side pseudonymization libraries to minimize sending direct identifiers. For high-risk PHI workflows we recommend pseudonymization at the proxy and then re-identification in a protected environment.

- Ingest guidance: avoid embedding identifiers in URLs; use POST JSON body and supply a tokenized patient_id. See attached ingest-architecture.png and sample-redaction-rules.txt for rule examples.

- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II summary and CAIQ export included. The DPA draft covers SCCs and standard clauses; legal should review the BAA appendix (we've left a redline-friendly section for customer-specific data retention & subprocessors).

If Aurelia wants a DPIA statement, we can produce a scoped DPIA summary focused on our processing activities and the controls above — we typically produce that within 5 business days.

Flagging dev: can you confirm the exact retention defaults for hosted PHI mode and whether we can offer a 30-day "do not persist" setting as the default for this customer?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inquiry: PHI proxying via Redwood hosted vs dedicated — evidence & DPA

Hi Samira — thanks again. Attached is the packet Kimberly assembled (SOC2 summary, CAIQ export, DPA draft, ingest architecture diagram and example redaction rules). Below is a short, actionable eligibility checklist and proposed next steps: 

Eligibility checklist (short):
- Hosted + BAA: allowed if you enable PHI mode in onboarding and sign our DPA/BAA (we've attached a draft).
- Retention controls: hosted offers "do not persist" full-text by default for PHI mode; you can request 30/90/180 day encrypted retention windows (we'll record selection in the DPA appendix).
- Dedicated/Private: recommended for high-volume PHI or if you require tenant-level telemetry separation or customer-managed networking/KMS.
- DLP + pseudonymization: use our sample-redaction-rules + client SDK to remove direct identifiers in the proxy before POSTing.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached DPA draft and indicate any redlines; legal@aurelia.health can send comments directly and we will route through our legal ops.
2) If helpful, book a 30-minute technical sync — I'm proposing Thu, May 27 at 10:00 AM PT. Is that OK? (If so we will invite our Security engineer and Solutions architect).
3) Tell us your desired retention window (do not persist / 30 / 90 / 180) so we can lock defaults into the DPA appendix.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/98765 (I pasted the HubSpot deal for reference).

If you want a DPIA scoped statement, we can produce that after we confirm the data elements and retention — estimate ~5 business days.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
SVP, Sales — Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
